steps.text: A piece of Originium crystal lies quietly on the test table, glowing orange-yellow under the light.
It looks pure, beautiful, harmless.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Priestess... What have we done...?

steps.name: Savage
steps.text: I'm afraid not. It's impossible.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Doctor... it hurts...

steps.name: Dying Infected
steps.text: Thank... you...
The Doctor picks up the Originium crystal with one hand and stabs it into the other arm.
It leaves a bloody gash on the arm, but nothing else.
The pain grows distinct.
Yet it is not the pain of Originium infection.
The instruments show the same: There is no sign of assimilation of Originium and cell.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: ...Originium won't infect me.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Did we ever imagine that such pain would come?

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: What would you say about what's happening to this world?

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: (Unknown language) Originium.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: (Unknown language) The last spark that we have passed on.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: (Steady breathing)

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: It's working.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: It's several times more effective than existing suppressants. Amiya's blood Originium crystal concentration has dropped significantly.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: But...

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: It's just a prototype. I haven't found a way to mass-produce it on Terra yet.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Doctor!

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I know you're experimenting on yourself... but you really don't look well.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Just some research on blood.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Originium doesn't infect me. We've had safety measures in place since it was just an energy project. Maybe this could be used to mitigate the symptoms of Oripathy.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: And Theresa... she's not like you. Civilight Eterna is not some kind of powerful magic. She has simply created Originium Arts in its most fundamental form, through the accumulation of a long legacy.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: With her help, we may be able to develop more advanced Oripathy medicine that can be mass produced...

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I'm more concerned about you right now, Doctor.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: I'm fine.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: If Originium has transformed you into beings identical to us, then there will be a way to create a serum in place of my own...

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: No matter how complicated the present issues are, if Babel can develop an effective Oripathy medicine...

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: It will be more than just the Sarkaz that support us. It will be all of Terra.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Then, we can—

a.text: Foster a future with Originium, one that is peaceful, happy, and eternal.

spans.text: Foster a future with Originium, one that is peaceful, happy, and eternal.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: No, listen to me.
Kal'tsit grabs the Doctor's arm.
It is a lot thinner than she remembers.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: You have not relaxed for an instant, from Rim Billiton, to the Sarkaz civil war.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I chose to wake you up in order to point the way for this civilization, one that's surprised me at every turn.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I don't want you to waste away now.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: You need to take care of yourself.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: ...Sorry.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Right now, though, what I want to do most is alleviate Amiya's pain.
Three months later...
Rhodes Island of Babel, Kazdel

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: I see you, Amiya. You can come out.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Doctor... am I interrupting anything?

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: No, just curious how you got in when I didn't hear the door open.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I found a lot of secret passages.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Secret passages?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Yeah. Closure said not to tell anyone, so I haven't.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: No wonder Dr. Kal'tsit can't find you for checkups. You've been hiding there all along.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: ...I promise I won't run away, if you go with me.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Alright, I'll try to make the time.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: You've been really busy. Dr. Kal'tsit said even she has hardly seen you lately.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Whenever I see you, you're all by yourself, carrying a stack of papers, head down, walking from one end of a corridor to the other.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: If someone says hi to you, all you do is nod, then keep on walking without a word.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Sounds like you're describing a really rude person. Sorry, Amiya.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: No, that's not what I meant... you just seem really unhappy.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Why would you say that?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Before we came to Rhodes Island, you were curious about everything, cuddled up with the burdenbeasts at night, crouched down to look at tiny rocks in the mines, and went to pick fruit from beckbeast dens...

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: You enjoyed everything, even the things that didn't interest me as a kid.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: But now... whenever I talk to you about something fun, all you say is, 'I'm glad you enjoyed it, Amiya.'

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: But I came to talk to you about it to make you feel happy...

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Are you unhappy because I'm not getting better?

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: It's not because of you, Amiya. This is about me.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: And... you can hear noises outside the ship, can't you?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Yes. Like the huge drills in Rim Billiton. They're so noisy... I don't like them.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Me, Theresa, Dr. Kal'tsit, we all have a lot of things to do. It's not your fault.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: ...Alright.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Do you have time today, Amiya?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Yes!

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: I want to go up the deck and see the clouds. It's going to rain. They have very interesting shapes, and I could talk for a long time if there was someone there to listen to me.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Of course! But... don't you have work to do?

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: It's okay... I'll be done soon.

a.text: Amiya.
If there comes a day when we cure Oripathy, not just for you but for all of Terra as well...
When the day comes that Terrans no longer live in fear of Originium and Catastrophe...
Let's go on a journey again, to see the rest of this great land.
This time, we'll bring Kal'tsit, and...
Originium will become the light that guides the next civilization.
All consciousness shall foster new hope in Originium, until the end of time.

spans.text: All consciousness shall foster new hope in Originium, until the end of time.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Doctor!

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: ...It's okay. The Doctor just passed out on the deck due to exhaustion.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Thank goodness... it's not something serious.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: What about the wound on the Doctor's arm?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Trying to contract Oripathy. The Doctor tried many ways: breathing in dust, exposure to Originium-dense environments, even a direct incision with active Originium...

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I tried to get the Doctor to stop, and I asked Scout to do the same, but...

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: No one wants to see the Doctor get hurt.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Maybe the Doctor is in more pain than we see on the surface.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: What about Amiya?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Terribly frightened. She wouldn't stop crying. It took a lot of effort to get her to sleep.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: This is... a sculpture?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: A gift from a rescued Infected to the Doctor.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Ace was the first to hear Amiya's cry. He carried the Doctor back and left this behind.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: See, Doctor? You've established connections with so many people. You're not alone.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: But what are you hiding that you wouldn't even tell Kal'tsit or me?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: The Doctor truly wants to help Amiya and Babel. I can feel that.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: But I also can't help but feel that the Doctor leaves some thoughts unsaid... some concerns, some doubts.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: I believed these sentiments were the result of such an abrupt awakening, and that they would go away in time.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: But they haven't.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: The Doctor is being torn apart by these unsaid things, tormented by hesitation, pain, and guilt.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Perhaps I don't understand the Doctor as well as I thought.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I don't know how to ease the Doctor's pain. And if neither of us know what the Doctor is thinking...

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Then the Doctor of Babel will always be alone, all the love and respect notwithstanding.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: ...Kal'tsit.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I will explain to the Doctor in time.
Theresa puts her hand on the Doctor's forehead.
Under the warm surface lies a past that she cannot fathom.
Civilight Eterna.

a.text: Originium must rewrite all.
Only then is there value in existence.

spans.text: Only then is there value in existence.

a.text: From the emergence of intelligent life, to the lights in the cosmos and the maelstrom of the stars.
Originium will continue to replicate and transform, until even time ceases to exist.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: This... is Originium?

a.text: Originium.
The first light before the Big Bang.
She said that only by covering every inch of the land in Originium, only by returning matter and time, tide and wonder, light and wailing, to the vast ocean of information...
Only then will we find change and advancement, and avert the fate that is the end.
Even though...
It is not a transformation, but a death.
It is not an extinction, but a continuation.

spans.text: It is not an extinction, but a continuation.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: When was this memory...? The Doctor's emotion, pain, hesitation, and... fear?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Who was that... accompanying the Doctor in despair?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: No, Kal'tsit said there was another—
The growth of Originium is silent, beautiful, calm.
All signs of life have been overgrown, civilization has vanished from this land.
But Theresa feels only fear and suffocation.
The memory is trembling, collapsing. There is a force somewhere, trying to fix an error.
The Originium in the memory continues to grow, even assimilating Theresa's consciousness—
'Theresa...'
Kal'tsit? Oh, yes, she was by my side.
'Theresa!'
She seems to see the Doctor, before her consciousness is fully absorbed by the nebulous Originium light—

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Theresa!

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: What happened, Theresa?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: What did you see?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: I... I saw Originium.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: It had assimilated the entire continent. The Doctor felt pain and anxiety over it.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Was that the Doctor's memory? No... a dream?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Give me a hand, Kal'tsit. The feeling, the noise and the wailing... I...

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Theresa.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I told you that Originium once decided the distant future of this land. There were two choices.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: We were too focused on tangible suffering, Catastrophe, Oripathy. Casting our eyes toward that future brought too much difficulty and too little meaning.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The Doctor chose one of them... the future that the Doctor spoke of to me, personally.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I could not forget that future the Doctor described. Never, in all these years.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: But the other cold and empty thought has often shot up my spine in the middle of the night over the past ten thousand years.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I cannot speak of it.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: But you can sense my anger with your power.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: That means that Civilight Eterna exists outside of the boundaries of language.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: So, Theresa.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: If you saw a future that you are not willing to accept, I hope you, Civilight Eterna, can change the course. Only you can.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: If you saw the side of myself or the Doctor that is strange to you...

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Kal'tsit?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: No, Kal'tsit, that's not what I meant—

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: —The Doctor's feelings toward Amiya, toward us, toward you, are sincere. That is the truth.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Trust the Doctor, and trust me. I will find the answer to what is tormenting the Doctor. And when—

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Ugh...

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Doctor!

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Doctor... you're awake.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: What happened to me?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: You fainted as you were leaving the deck with Amiya.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Hgnh... where's Amiya?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: A little shaken, but she's fine.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: You're still in bad shape. What were you thinking?

a.text: I want to cure Amiya's Oripathy. I want to change the present state of the Sarkaz.

spans.text: I want to cure Amiya's Oripathy. I want to change the present state of the Sarkaz.

a.text: I want to walk among this civilization that I helped create, to take in the vitality of new life, something that we once had, but have long since lost.

spans.text: I want to walk among this civilization that I helped create, to take in the vitality of new life, something that we once had, but have long since lost.

a.text: Even if...
Even if everything that we see, all that we know, all that we cherish, no longer exists after a millennium.

spans.text: Even if everything that we see, all that we know, all that we cherish, no longer exists after a millennium.
